leyline.white:
White leyline mages are the shield-bearers of the line — wardens and oathkeepers whose power is unity rather than self. Stand beside a White mage and you are harder to hurt, harder to sway, and luckier on the dice; when you falter they answer, taking the blow, turning the failure, holding you at the edge of death. They rarely strike first. Nothing a White mage does works alone, and that is the point.

Their turns are spent in position and their best moments are answers: a shield stepped between an ally and the blade, half a wound taken in another's place, an enemy's hostile act made harder, an ally's failed roll made good. Every draw on the leyline tops up the formation.

White Specialties

The White leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Coordination. Making the party's rolls better — a pointed target raises the stakes for the next ally to test against it, one success hands the next a raised stake, an ally's Complication becomes a blank face — plus the line moved together, a condition lifted, and a small healing aura.

Bulwark. Adjacency made armor — free Deflect for whoever stands with you, less damage for every ally at your shoulder, a shield stepped in, a blow taken in another's place, retribution on the attacker, and the line that will not break.

Accord. Terms agreed with allies — a shared objective that steadies you both and your White modifier lent to whoever pursues it — and the discipline that makes influence cheaper to resist for everyone near you and leaves Disoriented whoever you out-argue.

Draw Mana: allies within Attunement Range regain Health equal to your Tier.
leyline.blue:
Blue leyline mages read the battle a beat before it happens. They never meet force with force — a Blue mage takes the slow turn, learns what an enemy means to do, and makes sure it goes badly: disadvantage on the roll that matters, a wall that was not there a moment ago, a double that takes the arrow meant for a friend. At the height of their art they can unmake a working as it is cast and hold an enemy where it stands. They deal no wounds. They do not need to.

A Blue mage's best tools are earned by being right: predict an enemy's action and gain a Reaction when it comes; build the barricade before the archer draws; hold the counterspell for the moment a rival draws on the leyline. Much of what Blue can do arrives at the third rank — until then it is a disadvantage engine with a barricade and a double.

Blue Specialties

The Blue leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Foresight. Knowing the next move — a prediction that pays in Reactions, an intent the GM reveals, a telepathic network that shares your expertise, and the right to change your turn after everyone else has chosen.

Calculation. Making the roll go wrong — disadvantage on the test that matters, again and again, the counterspell that unmakes a working as it is cast, and the suggestion that leaves the influenced Disoriented.

Illusion. Light and lie — a phantom double, a shimmering barricade with hit points of its own, a static image that later learns to walk, an unseen slick underfoot, and walls that close in until an enemy cannot move.

Draw Mana: gain Advantage on your next Cognitive test.
leyline.black:
Black leyline mages are predators, and the leyline feeds on them as they feed on their prey. Draw Mana and every enemy standing alone is Weakened; from there the Black mage bites harder, heals off the kill, and refuses to let the quarry rejoin its line. The power is paid for in the mage's own blood — the withering ray costs health, not Investiture — and the leyline pays the debt back in advantage, in reserve, and in stolen life. When one enemy must not act, it does not.

A Black mage picks the one who is alone, or makes one with a shove, and does not let go. The ray fires every Action for as long as the mage can bleed; the Weakened cannot come home to their friends; the dangerous one loses a turn to a single command. Every thought the enemy spends costs them more while a Black mage is near.

Black Specialties

The Black leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Isolation. Punishing the lone and the separated — the shove that breaks a formation, the hex that Weakens whoever stands alone, the bite that lands harder on the Weakened and pays Investiture back, and a dread presence that keeps them from ever rejoining their line.

Ritual. Power bought with blood — a withering ray and a dark investiture that cost health rather than Investiture, advantage and a stored reserve returned for every drop, and a predator's due on the kill.

Subjugation. Seizing the mind — a hollow command that takes an enemy's whole turn, a tax on every thought they spend, and at the last the puppeteer who chooses the actions of the depleted.

Draw Mana: enemies within range with no ally within 5 ft become Weakened.
leyline.red:
Red leyline mages burn hotter the longer a fight goes on. Every blow struck near a Red mage — theirs or anyone's — feeds a rising edge the whole party shares, and every Fast turn is faster than the last. Play it as a pyromancer whose bolts arc and spread and leave the ground smouldering, or as a charger who hits hardest at the end of a run and never stops moving. Either way the guard is already down: drawing on the Red leyline costs your Reaction, and nothing in this tree will give it back.

A Red mage takes the Fast turn, draws for advantage, and spends it — from range, with bolts that arc to a second target and surges that catch a crowd; or up close, with the charge that hits harder for the distance covered and the slam that ends against a wall. The party stands near, because everything that happens near a Red mage makes their next roll better.

Red Specialties

The Red leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Momentum. Force that compounds — the reckless advance, the strike that hits harder after a run, the leap that flattens the landing, the slam into a wall, and the charger who keeps moving after every blow on a Fast turn.

Conflagration. Pyromancy unleashed — the searing bolt, the arc to a second target, the surge that catches a crowd, kindling that makes every burn brighter, the afterburn, and the chain that detonates through whatever stands beside the fallen.

Frenzy. The fight's heat as a weapon — a rising bonus the whole party shares for every blow struck near you, enemies incited to swing at whoever is nearest, and punishments for the confident, the failing, and the twice-struck.

Draw Mana: gain Advantage on your next Physical test, but lose your Reaction until your next turn.
leyline.green:
Green leyline mages belong to the wild's logic. Wardens, menders and pack-leaders, they grow the ground against their enemies — roots that hold, thorns that bite, and a territory that spreads with every draw — and they knit deep wounds that lesser magic cannot touch: Green is the only leyline that closes an Injury. And they hunt as a pack. The more of you land on one quarry, the harder each blow falls, and a Green mage always knows which one is weakest.

A Green mage draws where the enemy has to walk, roots the dangerous one, and points the pack at the weakest. The mending answers by itself when an ally drops to half, and between fights it repairs what nothing else can.

Green Specialties

The Green leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Territory. Owning the ground — difficult terrain that spreads, thorns that bite whoever enters it, roots that Restrain, and no leaving without the warden's leave.

Restoration. Deep mending — a touch that heals, a Reaction that answers a falling ally, regrowth that keeps giving, conditions lifted, and the only leyline healing that closes an Injury.

Instinct. The pack's edge — advantage for two who close on the same prey, blows that land harder for every hunter on the same target, the pack moved as one body, the weakest always known, and prey driven into the packmates' reach.

Draw Mana: create difficult terrain at a point within Attunement Range.

deity.Life:
Anaveth, the Vital Hand, is the deity of Life — growth, healing, and the intimate knowledge of living things. Her disciple diagnoses first: one look at an enemy and the whole company knows where it is weakest and cuts deeper for it, and every wound it takes pays her power back. She spends that power on healing no leyline mender can match — floods that leave vigor behind, hide that hardens, regeneration that does not stop — and, in time, on grafting adaptations onto an ally that make them the battle's engine.

A disciple of Anaveth marks the enemy the party is going to fight anyway, and from then on the fight funds itself; each heal carries a rider chosen for the moment. The mutations are the deep end of the path — bone, venom, dense tissue, and at the last the apex form that makes one creature a regenerating, armored engine for the scene and leaves it with an Injury after.

Signature resources: Diagnosis — a scene-long reading of one creature that sharpens the whole party against it and pays you back as it bleeds; Mutation — a lasting biological boon grafted onto an ally (bone spurs, venom, dense tissue) for the scene, reached at the path's deep end.

Requires attunement to both Blue and Green leylines.
deity.Knowledge:
Gnothis, the Watching Mind, is the deity of Knowledge — but his is the knowledge of the hunt. To study a thing is to learn how to kill it. His disciple marks one quarry and watches it: every turn's study is another Insight upon it, and every Insight makes the next blow heavier — for the disciple and for the whole pack, who see what he sees and profit from it. The kill does not end the study. It carries it to the next.

A disciple of Gnothis marks on the first turn and then strikes the same creature every turn after, the number growing as it goes; the pack piles on because the pack is paid for it. The verdict — the whole stack spent in one blow — is a finisher, not the plan.

Signature resource: Insight — an accumulating mark of study on a quarry; each stack sharpens the damage you and your pack deal to it.

Requires attunement to both Red and Green leylines.
deity.Civilization:
Kethane, the Great Builder, is the deity of Civilization — the forge, the wall, and the bonds that turn a crowd into a community. Her disciple builds. On the first turn a Combat Construct stands up and fights beside the company for the scene, and every talent after arms it — a tempered edge, a siege form, a second strike, at last a Colossus. Around it she lays Foundations: ground that steadies whoever holds it, roads allies can step between in an instant, and, when the enemy comes, walls with teeth.

A disciple of Kethane builds the machine first and lets it fight on its own initiative for free, then spends her own turns on the quarter — Foundations under the party, a road between them, walls when the enemy comes. A Construct that falls is not repaired; it is forged again.

Signature resources: Combat Construct — a persistent forged companion, armed by most of the path; Foundation — a designated square that steadies allies who hold it.

Requires attunement to both Red and White leylines.
deity.Chaos:
Maelith, the Unmaker of Certainties, is the deity of Chaos — patron of the broken plan and the fatal coincidence. Her disciple finds the fault line in an enemy's mind and marks it with an Omen, and every Omen is a crack waiting to be widened: into a good roll taken away at the worst moment, into solitude where no ally can help, into a working undone, into wounds no armor turns aside. When the pattern breaks, everything breaks with it.

A disciple of Maelith stamps first and spends second — an Omen on the target, another on its neighbour, and then, the moment one of them rolls the test that matters, the Omen is spent and the roll goes the other way. The disciple senses every marked enemy through walls and is paid Investiture each time one is hurt.

Signature resource: Omen — a fault line marked on an enemy when a Blue test lands; spent to force a reroll, to Isolate and wound, to Disorient and dispel, or shattered all at once for area spirit damage.

Requires attunement to both Blue and Black leylines.
deity.Death:
Morrath, the Last Harvest, is the deity of Death — not its terror but its husbandry. Every fall within her disciple's reach is an offering: it pays back Investiture and leaves a Harvested Remain, and Remains are the coin of her darker work — bone gardens, risen servants, answers wrung from the dead. Her curses wither and forbid healing; her decay feeds on the dying; her ward keeps one of hers from dying today. And at the last, the dead are made to rise whole.

A disciple of Morrath spends the first turns installing what will not stop — decay on the bloodied, a cascade that hurts every enemy near each new death, a garden where they will stand — and then reaps for free while the fight goes on. Corpses, not Investiture, are the true limit: the whole party's kills are her fuel.

Signature resource: Harvested Remain — a marker left on a corpse that drops within your range, spent to power Morrath's corpse-magic.

Requires attunement to both Black and Green leylines.
deity.Fate:
Olvarra, the Thread-Reader, is the deity of Fate — the one who has walked the battlefield before the battle. Her disciple builds the fight before the enemy understands it is being fought: Ordained Ground where allies will stand and be hard to touch, Snares on the squares an enemy has not yet chosen to enter, and threads between them so that a friend on one can spring the trap on another. She can read a foe's next step and move the wire into it. At the last she names an event, and when it comes, everything she prepared answers at once.

A disciple of Olvarra spends her Actions on the board and gives the results away: the allies standing on her ground do the striking, and the enemy walks into the damage. One reading of a foe's intent, and the trap slides into its path.

Signature resources: Ordained Ground — an ally-anchored square that fortifies whoever holds it; Snare — a single-use trap sprung by the first enemy to enter.

Requires attunement to both White and Green leylines.
deity.Power:
Tyrith, the Iron Crown, is the deity of Power — domination as an end in itself. His disciple does not persuade. One word and an enemy kneels, Compelled, its next choice his to make; defiance itself draws blood. In the press he is a warlord: every strike carries extra weight, a kill sends him forward, nothing slows the advance, and the more enemies he has broken this scene, the harder the next blow lands. His banner-bearers share the crown. He pays for it in his own spirit.

A disciple of Tyrith kneels the one who matters and commands him next turn, then advances through the line. Nothing here is ranged, nothing heals, nothing refunds: Investiture and spirit are spent, and the crown is paid for.

Signature resource: Warlord's Fury — for the scene, every melee blow lands heavier for each enemy the warlord has broken below half, and heavier again on the kill.

Requires attunement to both Black and Red leylines.
deity.Destruction:
Razkael, the Sundering Flame, is the deity of Destruction — the siege engineer and pyrotechnician who turns timing into devastation. His disciple sets Charges with a trigger of his choosing and detonates them when he likes; nothing dodges what was decided before it arrived. His fires do not go out — they spread, they follow the marked, they grow on every death — and when the moment is right, every Charge and every flame he has placed goes off at once.

A disciple of Razkael places, waits, and detonates. Almost nothing here can miss or be saved against; the enemy's one defence is not to stand where the disciple decided. The party's job is to keep them there.

Signature resources: Charge — a placed marker with a declared trigger that detonates for area energy damage and scars the ground; dangerous terrain — the fire left behind, which spreads, merges, and keeps burning.

Requires attunement to both Blue and Red leylines.
deity.Order:
Tessavain, the Lawgiver, is the deity of Order — patron of oath, pact and prohibition, whose word, once given, binds both ways. His disciple declares Edicts: one forbidden act, and the first enemy to commit it is struck by the law itself. And swears Covenants: a pact with an ally that shields them both for as long as neither breaks it. To keep his law is to be sheltered by it. To break it is to learn that the court does not adjourn for one defendant.

The lawgiver's lane and the oath-brother's lane run side by side. An Edict's finest outcome is that it never fires — an enemy who obeys is an enemy controlled — and when the disciple wants it to fire, a Verdict forces the violation and the punishment spreads. A Covenant makes two harder to kill than one, and a Concord makes the sworn a company.

Signature resources: Edict — a prohibition that punishes the forbidden action; Covenant — a sworn pact that fortifies both partners.

Requires attunement to both Blue and White leylines.
deity.Sovereignty:
Verdannis, the Crowned Arbiter, is the deity of Sovereignty — the right to raise and to cast down. His disciple rules on who may strike hard: with one word an enemy's blows shrink, die by die, and with another an ally's grow. The judgments begin as moments and become the law of the scene, and an enemy found wanting feeds the court — every failed swing pays the arbiter back, opens a Reactive Strike, or shields the company. Here, he decides what is possible.

A disciple of Verdannis chooses the enemy whose blows are feared and the ally whose blows are wanted, and rules on both; the rest of the fight is watching the diminished miss and collecting what each failure pays. The court's reach is one creature at a time.

Signature resource: Censure and Exalt — judgments on a creature's damage dice, stepping an enemy's down or an ally's up — for a round, and then for the scene.

Requires attunement to both Black and White leylines.

heroic.Hunter:
The thrill of the chase thrums in a Hunter's mind. A Hunter chooses one quarry at a time, and then everything sharpens against it — finding it, striking it, learning where it is weak. Archers shoot from range and step back out of reach. Assassins open with surprise and finish with one terrible stab. Trackers lay concealed traps and fight beside an animal companion that grows as they do. Almost nothing a Hunter does costs Investiture or focus: they never run dry, and they never needed the leylines.

Choose the quarry before the fight if you can, or with the first arrow if you cannot; set the trap where it will walk. Then it is patience: the shot and the step back into cover, the blade for the moment it looks away, the companion on the far flank.

Hunter Specialties

The Hunter path presents talents in three specialties:

Archer. Single-target marksmanship — longer reach and heavier arrows, the shot and the step out of reach, a reading of the quarry's weakest point, and, in time, arrow after arrow into the same mark.

Assassin. Knives and surprise — a jab that leaves the target Surprised, the fatal thrust on the unsuspecting, the quarry re-marked with every kill, and a second Dodge for the unarmored.

Tracker. The wilderness — a concealed trap that holds or bleeds whoever springs it, food and tools from the land, sure feet on bad ground, and an animal companion who lends its defence, guards an ally, and grows with every Tracker pick.

Building a Hunter

Consider these general tips for building an effective Hunter:

Attributes. It's usually a good idea to prioritize Awareness, Strength, and Speed.

Skills. Useful skills include Agility, Perception, Stealth, Survival, and either Light Weaponry or Heavy Weaponry.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.kWWyJQRYlIMoQCe9]{Warrior} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.qqa1ZgA957Cae6ex]{Agent} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can't go wrong with an animal companion — the Tracker specialty is built around one — and a fine ranged weapon.

Hunter Key Talent

The Hunter key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.3nfGn0BOeLq5qgEr]{Seek Quarry}, unlocks access to the Hunter specialties.

Starting Skill: Perception. If you choose Hunter as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Perception.
heroic.Envoy:
An Envoy's whole art is one gesture, endlessly refined: a word that leaves an ally Determined, and a lifetime of learning what else that word can carry. A Mentor delivers it on every strike for free. The Faithful make it restore focus, shake off a fall, steel a defence, and ripple resolve through the whole company. A Diplomat turns it on the enemy — a challenge that rattles them, a calm that settles them, and, if every foe is pacified, a fight that ends with no one dead. Envoys serve something larger than themselves, and shape it in the serving.

Hit something, or Gain Advantage, and the word goes out for free; choose the rider the moment needs — focus for the caster running dry, a defence for the one being hunted, a condition off the one knocked down. Keep the Reaction for the ally about to fail. Against enemies you would rather not kill: challenge, calm, and talk them down.

Envoy Specialties

The Envoy path presents talents in three specialties:

Diplomat. Force of personality turned on the enemy — a challenge that Disorients and rattles them, calm that pacifies them, and, if every foe is pacified, a fight that ends with no one dead; with the contacts to match in high society.

Faithful. Devotion as a discipline — the party's focus restored and every recovery made larger, a fall shaken off, a defence steeled, and resolve rippled through the whole company when one ally spends theirs.

Mentor. The word delivered free on every strike and every advantage gained — focus returned, a ward made Focused, a second Reaction each turn, an ally's advantage lent onward, and the fallen brought back to their feet.

Building an Envoy

Consider these general tips for building an effective Envoy:

Attributes. It's usually a good idea to prioritize Presence and Willpower.

Skills. Discipline is an essential skill for most Envoys. Other useful skills include Deception, Leadership, Lore, and Persuasion.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.spF8y5TmLUxxMfxm]{Leader} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.oFA1jJZQMhTUjyem]{Scholar} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can't go wrong with influential patrons — High Society Contacts needs one — and a companion to mentor.

Envoy Key Talent

The Envoy key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.l4wRQT2MH0SsxmRQ]{Rousing Presence}, unlocks access to the Envoy specialties.

Starting Skill: Discipline. If you choose Envoy as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Discipline.
heroic.Warrior:
Warriors fight in stances — a way of standing chosen for the scene and changed in a heartbeat — and everything else they know rides on the Strike. A Duelist reads an opponent, breaks their nerve, and ends the broken. A Leybreaker fights the lines themselves: always knows when someone draws, hits the breath they were holding, makes every working near them cost blood, and carries no magic and needs none. A Soldier braces, shares the brace with the whole line, and lands the blow that ends the argument.

Pick the stance for the scene, then Strike and spend focus on the rider that fits — drain their focus, shove them, tax their Investiture. When the target's focus hits zero, end them. The heaviest blows arrive with the third rank of a skill; before that the Strike and a Warrior's free damage riders are plenty.

Warrior Specialties

The Warrior path presents talents in three specialties:

Duelist. Flame, Iron and Vine stances, a feint that takes an opponent's focus and Reaction, and the execute — a strike on the emptied that ignores armor and cannot graze; a signature weapon and quick feet.

Leybreaker. Some warriors learn to fight the lines themselves. A Leybreaker holds the ground a working needs, closes before it lands, and makes every point of Investiture cost blood, carrying no magic and needing none.

Soldier. The line — training in weapon and armor, Brace made twice as good and shared with everyone behind your shield, the heavy two-Action blow, a second Strike, and never being Surprised while you have focus.

Building a Warrior

Consider these general tips for building an effective Warrior:

Attributes. It's usually a good idea to prioritize Speed and Strength, then consider Awareness and Willpower.

Skills. Useful skills include Athletics, Light Weaponry, Heavy Weaponry, Intimidation, Leadership, and Persuasion.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.spF8y5TmLUxxMfxm]{Leader} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.E6O5QgdG1JxA7tnf]{Hunter} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. Nothing in the Warrior path waits on a reward: a good weapon and armor you can wear all day are the whole kit.

Warrior Key Talent

The Warrior key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.8mJC2HnsN3OQ2J20]{Vigilant Stance}, unlocks access to the Warrior specialties.

Starting Skill: Athletics. If you choose Warrior as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Athletics.
heroic.Scholar:
A Scholar's knowledge is a tool the whole party uses. Erudition lets a Scholar rewrite their own skills between rests to fit what is coming. A Ley-surveyor reads the leylines as a landscape — who is attuned, when they draw, what a draw will do — and lends that certainty to allies while making enemy workings cost more. A Strategist hands the right advantage to the right person at the right moment and, once a scene, gives everyone an extra Action. A Surgeon heals without Investiture and brings the fallen back. A Scholar deals no wounds; a Scholar decides who does.

Between rests, set the skill list for what is coming. In a fight, act late — your defences are up until you do — Gain Advantage and hand it to the striker, mark the ground under the party's mage, and keep Field Medicine ready as a Free Action. Against a leyline mage, read the draw and tax the working.

Scholar Specialties

The Scholar path presents talents in three specialties:

Ley-surveyor. The leylines are a landscape, and a Ley-surveyor reads it: where the lines pool, who is drawing on them, and what a draw will do before it happens. Where others build devices, a surveyor builds certainty and lends it to whoever stands beside them.

Strategist. Timing — advantage handed to the ally who needs it and the target denied its Reactions against them, defences raised until you have acted, an ally's Complication removed, skills reassigned mid-adventure, and, once a scene, an extra Action for the whole party.

Surgeon. The clinic — a heal that costs focus rather than Investiture, made a Free Action and grown by Medicine and Lore, an exhausting jab, injury conditions treated during a rest, and the unconscious or the recently dead brought back.

Building a Scholar

Consider these general tips for building an effective Scholar:

Attributes. It's usually a good idea to prioritize Intellect above all else, then Presence plus either Speed or Strength (depending on your desired combat functionality).

Skills. Useful skills include Deduction, Lore, and Medicine.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.qqa1ZgA957Cae6ex]{Agent} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.axOgzq972lY7la00]{Envoy} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can't go wrong with library access — Erudition reassigns after a long rest with one — and a companion to mentor.

Scholar Key Talent

The Scholar key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.8FYBJZC8PBjneOim]{Erudition}, unlocks access to the Scholar specialties.

Starting Skill: Lore. If you choose Scholar as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Lore.
heroic.Agent:
Agents grasp the threads of fate. Where others roll the plot die and hope, an Agent rerolls it, turns a Complication into an Opportunity, raises the stakes on purpose, and lends the trick to a friend — and when a scene needs three things done at once, focus buys the time. Investigators read motives and close cases. Spies live under cover and disappear behind it. Thieves gamble, jab, and vanish. Rules from outside are playthings; Agents answer only to their own code.

Take the risk on purpose: raise the stakes, and if the die comes up wrong, reroll it or spend focus to make the Complication an Opportunity. Buy actions when a scene needs three skill tests in one turn. In a fight, Stun the one who matters and get out of reach; out of one, be whoever the room needs.

Agent Specialties

The Agent path presents talents in three specialties:

Investigator. Motives and deduction — learn what a target wants and leverage it, become Focused on a success, know when they lie, and, once the case is built, make them back down.

Spy. Cover — a false identity, a disguise that needs no supplies and Surprises whoever sees through it, a silent takedown that leaves the target unable to call out, and contacts in high society.

Thief. The gamble — stakes raised on purpose, a jab that Stuns, a vanish after the Disengage, quick feet, and contacts in the criminal underworld.

Building an Agent

Consider these general tips for building an effective Agent:

Attributes. It's usually a good idea to prioritize Awareness, Intellect, and Speed.

Skills. Useful skills include Agility, Deception, Deduction, Insight, Light Weaponry, and Thievery.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.E6O5QgdG1JxA7tnf]{Hunter} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.oFA1jJZQMhTUjyem]{Scholar} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can't go wrong with a bodyguard companion and patrons from the criminal world or high society.

Agent Key Talent

The Agent key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.ScqSKbkewDAfSizP]{Opportunist}, unlocks access to the Agent specialties.

Starting Skill: Insight. If you choose Agent as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Insight.
heroic.Leader:
Leaders decide who rolls well. The command die — a bonus die handed to an ally for the test that matters, grown larger with every Leader pick and delivered free after a Strike — is the whole of the path, and the rest is what a Leader does with rank. Champions draw fire and stay standing. Officers keep the line supplied, moving, and striking together. Politicos win with rumour, ruse, and enemies turned on each other. No path has more leverage over people, in a fight or out of one; and no path depends more on the title and the patron a campaign is willing to grant.

Strike, then hand the die to whoever is about to roll the test that decides the round. Move to draw fire; give the archer a free Disengage. Out of combat, no path has more leverage over people — rumour, deception, persuasion, command, all with a die on top.

Leader Specialties

The Leader path presents talents in three specialties:

Champion. Grit at the front — an intervention that draws an enemy's ire off your allies, enemies who resist you left Disoriented, more health, and a last stand that keeps you on your feet.

Officer. Order in the chaos — allies who Disengage or Gain Advantage as a Reaction, a command die that also moves and unslows, supplies requisitioned, and the synchronized assault where the line strikes together.

Politico. Rumour and ruse — an enemy's Reaction taken and their next test spoiled, scandal spread, a ruse that changes a detail, and enemies set at odds with one another.

Building a Leader

Consider these general tips for building an effective Leader:

Attributes. It's usually a good idea to prioritize Presence, Strength, and Willpower.

Skills. Useful skills include Athletics, Deception, Heavy Weaponry, Intimidation, Leadership, and Persuasion.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.kWWyJQRYlIMoQCe9]{Warrior} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.axOgzq972lY7la00]{Envoy} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can't go wrong with a mount companion, a patron (Rumormonger needs one), and a title granting command of five or more people (Authority needs it, and a third of the path waits on it).

Leader Key Talent

The Leader key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.UEaOm4P2UFcrP1Z8]{Decisive Command}, unlocks access to the Leader specialties.

Starting Skill: Leadership. If you choose Leader as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Leadership.
